newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude steady but Dated Brent faces losses.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude steady but Dated Brent faces losses.

text.p: North Sea crudes were broadly steady early on Monday but benchmark Dated Brent was set to fall as a trader looked to sell late August barrels back into Europe.
Oct Brent on the IPE shed 12 cents to $18.87 a barrel by 1120 GMT, tracking weaker U.S. markets, but intermonth cash spreads were little changed from late Friday levels.

Sep/Oct was pegged at -12/-8 cents and Oct/Nov at -15/-12 cents. Brent CFDs were also flat, with the next three weeks talked at Oct -30/-25 cents and trade limited to early Sept 2-8 dates at Oct -27 cents.
But Dated Brent was already showing signs of easing from Friday's traded levels of Sept Brent -8 and Oct Brent -15 cents.
"There's an offer indicated at Oct Brent -20 cents, and we have showed what a real refinery outlet would be prepared to pay Sept Brent -35 cents," said a trader.
A Wall Street trader holding four Brents loading Aug 26-30 was expected to sell at least one cargo.
"We've been told he'll move one today," said another trader.
Two Sept 2-4 Brent cargoes were due to turn wet on Monday, including a clocked Sept 1-3 deferred by Cargill.
Other North Sea crudes were steady, underpinned by solid refinery margins in northwest Europe and high freight rates which was seen helping Norwegian offshore loading grades.

In the Mediterranean, sour Urals talk was slow but traders said a couple of smaller cargoes were being offered at around Dated Brent -85 cents a barrel, basis cif Augusta, about 10 cents firmer than large cargoes.
"Small cargoes are definitely commanding a premium because there's plenty of competition from Kirkuk for the larger vessels," said one.
